rounds.what: The round's own observation from round 8 became code: an option-shaped stem is refused. Two texts the change had made false were corrected, and the class search behind them was re-derived and its fourth hit confirmed against the repository's own standard for marking a retired section.
Four checks: the skill sentence against the daemon's own branch, the generated mirror compared rather than rebuilt, the swept texts, and a refusal message that changed a string main owns.

The rig run against both halves, three sentences read against their paths rather than their predecessors, the fixture inversion stated at its real strength, and the daemon package's gap closed rather than stated: it runs here against a Postgres on this issue's own volume.

implementerProof.how: Round 11: I ran the rig's vector suite myself at this head and then restored the aliasing in an out-of-tree copy to see all nine fail, rather than taking the author's report of 9 of 9; I read each of the three corrected sentences against the code path it describes (Runtime.Release's call to releaseControllerSandbox, check.go's two IssueSuspend enqueue sites, podsafety's controller exception) rather than against the sentence it replaced; and I checked the claim that the daemon package cannot run here instead of recording it, which is how it turned out to be a Postgres rather than Docker. Rounds 1 to 10 were each verified as those rounds record.

proof.criterion: A merged close keeps the implementer's pod for the production check's first look, and the skill that teaches an architect so is true of the daemon.
proof.surface: The daemon's own workflow code, read against the sentence the change wrote.
proof.command: Read `packages/daemon/internal/workflow/linger.go:78-101` and `check.go` around its IssueSuspend enqueues; read `skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:416-420`
proof.observed: `linger.go` sets `except = claim.RoleImplementer` when `merged` and enqueues the `IssueSuspend` only inside `if !merged`, so a merged close takes five of six claims and queues no suspension; `check.go:261` and `:293` are where a pending look enqueues it. The skill says the implementer is left running, its pod stays for the first look, and the Sandbox goes only when a look reports pending. Sentence and code agree.
proof.negativeControl: The `!merged` branch is the control in the code itself: a close that is not a merge still queues the suspension, so the exception is the merged path's and not a removal of the behaviour.

proof.criterion: The generated copy of the skill matches its source.
proof.command: `diff skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md`, and the same for the worker skill
proof.observed: Identical, and the worker skill's mirror identical too.
proof.negativeControl: The worker skill is the control: a comparison that reports identical for a file nobody regenerated this round shows the method can distinguish, since both mirrors are kept by the same build and either could have drifted.

proof.criterion: A refusal message that stopped naming `pvc` must not have stopped refusing it.
proof.surface: The real `legion start --check-config` CLI built from this head.
proof.command: Five files: an unknown kind, `pvc`, the key omitted, `cloudsql-iam`, and the example
proof.observed: The unknown kind is told `must be 'postgres' or 'cloudsql-iam'` — the set a deployment may actually use. `pvc` and the omitted key still take their own rule, with the INFRA-80 reason naming `pvc` and the omitted key together. `cloudsql-iam` and the example load. Nothing in source asserts the old wording; the one grep hit is `docs/site/.bin/legion`, a committed compiled binary carrying it as build output.
proof.negativeControl: The previous round's binary, run first, still prints the old three-kind string — which is both the control that the message really changed and the reason the check is only valid from a binary built at this head.

proof.criterion: The stale-prose class, re-derived with a union of search terms rather than my own.
proof.command: grep the union `with its volume|transcript on the volume|sessions on the volume|two containers` beside the earlier `detach|outlives|ReadWriteOnce`, and read every hit
proof.observed: Two sites survive in files this change owns: `workflow/merge_close_test.go:215` and `daemon/outbox_issue_suspend_test.go:657`, each saying a Sandbox is released 'with its volume'. Both are a comment and a failure message rather than behaviour. Every other hit is correct: the repository cache and the controller do own volumes, and `docs/kubernetes.md:5183` names the file store in the past tense.
proof.negativeControl: The correct hits are the control on the search: a union that returned only false positives, or only the sites already fixed, would say nothing about coverage.

proof.criterion: The rig this change introduced gives an ephemeral volume a disk of the pod's own, and the vectors it carries detect what they claim to.
proof.surface: The rig's own suite in `internal/runtime/sandbox`, run in this pod.
proof.command: `go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox -run TestWhatAnIssuePlantsNeitherReadsTheProvisioningTokenNorOutlivesItsPod -count=1 -v`, at this head and again with the aliasing restored in an out-of-tree copy
proof.observed: 9 of 9 pass at this head. With `case volume.Ephemeral != nil: dir = rig.tree` restored — the aliasing the change removed — 9 of 9 fail. The copy was restored afterwards.
proof.negativeControl: The aliased rig is the control, and it is the item: a vector suite that passes here and was never run against the aliased rig would show only that it compiles.

proof.criterion: Each of the three corrected sentences is true of the path it describes.
proof.surface: The daemon's own code, read path by path.
proof.command: Read `supervise/table.go:1114-1124` against `Runtime.Release` (`sandbox.go:769-780`) and `releaseControllerSandbox`; the skill's close paragraph against every `IssueSuspend{` enqueue in `workflow/check.go`; `podsafety.go:12-20` against the controller's pod
proof.observed: `Release` suspends the locator, forgets the claim and calls `releaseControllerSandbox`, which deletes a Sandbox only where the store holds it as the controller's — so the comment's 'it deletes no issue Sandbox' is true. `IssueSuspend` is enqueued at exactly two sites, `check.go:261` in `endLookPending` and `:293` in `closeCheck` beside the `issue_close`, which is the three-way entry the skill now names instead of making `pending` exclusive. `podsafety` scopes its claim to the probe's pod and an issue's and excepts the controller's pod, which does mount a Sandbox-owned volume.
proof.negativeControl: The controller is the control in all three: it is the one pod whose disk does outlive it, so a sentence that still claimed no pod mounts such a disk would be caught by it, and `releaseControllerSandbox` is the path that makes the first sentence's 'only the controller's' exact rather than rhetorical.

proof.criterion: The daemon package's tests that use the inverted fixture run, pass, and each still fails for its own reason.
proof.surface: `go test ./internal/daemon` in this pod, against a PostgreSQL 16.2 unpacked onto this issue's own volume and started on 127.0.0.1:55432.
proof.command: `LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion@127.0.0.1:55432/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/daemon -run 'TestAChildClosedDoneDeletesItsSandboxWhileItsParentRuns|TestIssueCloseDeletesTheSandboxAfterARestart|TestTheSweepDeletesACarriedChildsOwnSandboxOnceItLeavesTheLine' -count=1 -v`, then once per mutation
proof.observed: All three run and pass. Neutering `SuspendIssue`'s `deleteStoredSandbox` reddens the first two and leaves the third green, because the sweep deletes through `ReconcileOrphans`; neutering the orphan sweep's own `deleteFenced` reddens the third, which is green again once restored. The claim that the package needs Docker was half right: the skip names `LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN`, and only `TestABootWaitsOutAGitHubRequestThatNeverAnswers` needs rootless Docker.
proof.negativeControl: Each mutation is its own negative control, and the one that failed to redden a test is the sharpest: it showed the mutation had missed that test's path rather than the test being weak.

proof.criterion: The fixture inversion keeps the architectural split between an issue's Sandbox and the controller's.
proof.command: Read `issueSandbox` in `outbox_issue_suspend_test.go`; read `claimTemplates` from `testdata/golden/{controller,controller-resume,worker}.json`; then put the superseded shape back into the fixture and re-run the three tests
proof.observed: `issueSandbox` builds `spec: {operatingMode: Running}` with no claim template, and `pvcs`/`pvc` are `disks`/`disk`. Both controller goldens still carry `claimTemplates: ['issue']` and the worker golden carries none, so the rename did not erase the split. With the superseded shape restored, all three tests still pass.
proof.negativeControl: The restored superseded shape is the control, and its result is the honest half: the inversion adds no test power, it makes the fixture say what the runtime builds.

observations: The previous round's binary still prints the pre-change refusal, and I ran it before noticing. Rebuilding from the head under test is the fourth instance today of the same discipline — verify the instrument is the one the question is about before reading what it says.

Round 11, the same rule a fifth time and twice over: `go test -run <one test>` printed `ok` in 0.026s and `-v` showed `--- SKIP`, so an unrun test looked like a passing one; and a mutation of `SuspendIssue`'s delete left the sweep's test green because that test deletes through `ReconcileOrphans`, another path. A test that survives a mutation is a question, and both times the answer was my instrument rather than the test.
notReachedHere: The seven inverted Stage 4a per-check assertions are unrun, not passing, and Stage 4b has run at no head — eleven readings of that harness have now found defects in it and nothing of it has been executed.

One test of `internal/daemon`, TestABootWaitsOutAGitHubRequestThatNeverAnswers, needs rootless Docker and panics, which takes an unfiltered package run down with it. That is the package's remaining limit: one test, not the package, and not the fixture tests this round checked.
Nothing this round ran against the cluster namespace. The admission policy there refused a scratch Postgres Job, saying a smaller build runs in its Legion pod, and that is what I did.
residualRisks: Unchanged from round 5: the single generation counter behind the gap record; a daemon restarting inside the replacement's gap; the stable claim name meaning a replacement pod waits on its predecessor's claim being reaped.
Unchanged from round 7: `production_audit`'s unguarded evidence write at `:2669`, pre-existing and left to the reviewer.

findingsNotFailures.what: Round 10's finding is fixed in this round, and its claim is now stated at its real strength.
findingsNotFailures.evidence: `issueSandbox` builds no claim template and `pvcs`/`pvc` are `disks`/`disk`; both controller goldens keep `claimTemplates: ['issue']` against the worker golden's none, so the rename did not erase the architectural split. Putting the superseded shape back into the fixture leaves all three tests passing.
findingsNotFailures.verdict: The inversion adds no test power: it makes the fixture say what the runtime builds, and the risk I named in round 10 is closed by construction rather than by any assertion. Each of the three tests was separately mutation-checked and pins its own reason — two reddened by neutering SuspendIssue's delete, the third by neutering the orphan sweep's own deleteFenced.
